source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Set the Thermal shutdown in the BIOS to Enabled/Disabled by following the below procedure:
    i) Navigate to System Utilities after the POST.
    ii) Navigate to System Utilities-> System Configuration-> System Options-> RBSU-> Advanced Options-> Fan and Thermal Options-> Thermal Shutdown.
    iii) Select the "Thermal Shutdown" and press "Enter" for a dialog box to open.
    iv) In the Dialog box, select "Enabled/Disabled" option. Save the settings by pressing "F10".
2. remove fan1
3. insert fan1
4. remove fan2 and fan3
5. insert fan2 and fan3
6. remove others fan
7. insert all fan

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL captures a one-fan/peer-speed concept, but it omits the BIOS Thermal Shutdown state, fan2+fan3 and `others` combinations, insertion events, shutdown/non-shutdown outcomes and recovery; its `-P` credentials are unsafe.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly keeps physical handling manual while requiring a BIOS phase decision, fan/zone map, supported removal combinations and independent cooling recovery.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 809/2291 repeats PARTIAL and a single-fan grep despite the Master multi-fan procedure; it provides no phase-specific acceptance or thermal-shutdown safety controls.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-974 draft was inspected only as history; this review independently separates BIOS-state and removal-combination axes, treats fan1-only Criteria as incomplete rather than invented coverage, and adds strict protection for the disabled-shutdown phase.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 preserves actual single/multiple fan removal and BIOS-state coverage, ED-36 treats the Project phase/combination matrix as readiness rather than permanent blocking, and ED-38 keeps BIOS changes, physical actions and DUT verdicts engineer-owned.

original_test_intent: Evaluate system fan redundancy and BMC logging across an approved Thermal Shutdown BIOS state and a sequence of fan-removal populations: fan1 alone, fan2+fan3 together and the remaining supported fan set, then restore every fan. The Master Criteria explicitly cover only Disabled/fan1 non-shutdown and fan1 remove/insert logs, so additional combinations need Project Expected Results without rewriting source.
original_method: Use the specified RBSU path to select and save Thermal Shutdown Enabled or Disabled, then physically remove/reinsert fan1, fan2+fan3 and other fans. Observe removal/insertion logs and whether the host remains operating; all BIOS and fan actions are operator-controlled.
manual_activity: A qualified operator changes and verifies the BIOS Thermal Shutdown state, removes/inserts only approved fan modules in the specified combinations, observes physical seating and LEDs, and restores the original BIOS state. Automation may collect mapped RPM/PWM, temperatures, SEL, power and host evidence.
required_inputs: Project decision whether Disabled only is authoritative or Enabled and Disabled are separate phases, with expected shutdown/non-shutdown behavior and approved final/restored BIOS value
Physical fan1/fan2/fan3/others slot, module/FRU, connector, controller channel, cooling zone, RPM/PWM/status SDR and redundancy-group map
Vendor hot-swap support and maximum supported simultaneous removals per zone, exact order/timing and interpretation of `remove others fan`
Per BIOS-state and removal-combination Expected Values for remaining-fan command/RPM, temperatures, assert/deassert or remove/insert events, host continuity/shutdown and recovery
System workload, independent thermal/power/fan monitoring, hard aborts, OOB/serial recovery, protected BMC access, operator and evidence clock
safety_requirements: Do not disable Thermal Shutdown or remove any fan until the approved state/combination matrix and an independent hard-stop owner exist.
Treat fan1, fan2+fan3 and `others` as distinct cooling failures; never infer that one-fan tolerance authorizes a simultaneous multi-fan state.

Map each physical fan before removal and use the vendor latch/hot-swap procedure; do not pull a non-hot-swappable module, disturb adjacent cables or leave an empty slot longer than the approved bound.

During a Disabled phase, BIOS protection is intentionally unavailable: use independent critical-component temperatures, target/peer RPM, power and host monitoring with conservative aborts that do not depend on BMC shutdown logic.

Abort on rapid/local thermal rise, unexpected peer response, remaining-fan failure/overspeed, shutdown, OOB loss or wrong event; reinsert the required fan set immediately and do not retry automatically.

Export baseline logs before any approved clear and preserve first failure evidence. Reinsert/secure all modules and prove airflow, RPM, temperatures, events and host health recover before another combination.
Restore the approved final Thermal Shutdown value and verify readback after any required reboot; do not leave the protection setting changed.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, validate the BIOS, fan/zone and combination package without changing DUT state.
After approval, capture BIOS state/readback, mapped fan RPM/PWM/status, component/zone temperatures, power, SEL/BMC and host continuity around engineer actions.
Produce separate results for each authorized BIOS-state and fan-removal combination; do not extend fan1-only source Criteria to fan2+fan3 or `others` without the approved Project matrix.
Do not navigate/change BIOS, remove/insert fans, control power, expose credentials, clear logs, retry or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the BIOS-state scope, final restore state, fan/zone mapping, supported single/multiple combinations and per-combination acceptance matrix.
Perform/supervise BIOS and fan actions with independent monitoring, physical seating checks, abort and emergency restoration.
Verify all fans and protection settings are restored and issue per-phase/per-combination plus overall DUT verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A one-fan RPM grep is only partial evidence: it cannot cover the source BIOS state, simultaneous fan2+fan3 or `others` removal, insert events or shutdown semantics; plaintext `-P` credentials are rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After approval, retain the source's operator BIOS/removal sequence and collect protected read-only mapped fan, temperature, SEL and host telemetry for each authorized phase; no single generic grep is sufficient.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The exact RBSU Thermal Shutdown path, Enabled/Disabled wording, fan1, fan2+fan3 and `others` sequence, Disabled/fan1 no-shutdown and remove/insert Criteria, no Script and 30/30-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.status: CONDITIONAL ON PHASE AND COMBINATION MATRIX
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Baseline and set the approved BIOS phase; under bounded load remove/reinsert each vendor-supported fan combination with mapped telemetry and events; hard-abort and restore on thermal limits; verify recovery after every combination; restore BIOS protection and cleanly read back.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BIOS/RBSU implementation, chassis fan population, cooling-zone redundancy and hot-swap design.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC/CPLD/fan-controller/SDR firmware, chassis/fan FRU and telemetry-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform Thermal Shutdown behavior, fan hot-swap/redundancy/combination limits, thermal envelope and BMC event specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds a two-axis BIOS-state/removal matrix, independent protection during Disabled and complete restoration evidence while preserving the source's physical sequence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Testing only Disabled/fan1 covers the explicit Criteria but not the Procedure's Enabled option or multi-fan combinations; any Project-scoped omission must be reported rather than called full coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: BIOS phase, fan map/combinations, Expected Results, thermal envelope, recovery and approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Simultaneous fan2+fan3 removal can eliminate a local cooling zone even if other chassis fans accelerate, especially while Thermal Shutdown is disabled.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may limit execution to vendor-supported combinations or a single BIOS state, but must preserve all original options/steps, identify N/A versus untested coverage and never use single-fan telemetry to claim multi-fan redundancy coverage.
expected_evidence: Approved BIOS-state/removal matrix, final restore value and fan1/fan2/fan3/others physical/zone/sensor applicability map
Vendor combination/hot-swap limits, workload and thermal margins, independent aborts, OOB path and operator authorization
Per-phase BIOS setting/save/readback plus baseline target/peer RPM/PWM, temperatures, power, SEL/BMC and host state
Per-combination physical removal/insertion timestamps, remaining-fan response, zone/component temperatures, host shutdown/non-shutdown and expected assert/deassert or remove/insert events
All fans secured with recovered RPM/airflow/temperatures/events/host health after every combination
Restored/read-back Thermal Shutdown setting, unexpected-event review, scope gaps and engineer-owned verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets Thermal Shutdown-controlled fan redundancy, but Procedure offers Enabled/Disabled and multiple removal combinations while Criteria explicitly cover only Disabled/fan1. This is incomplete Project acceptance coverage that can be resolved by an approved phase/combination matrix without AI choosing a contradictory core target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The BIOS setting, physical operations and explicit fan1 acceptance are identifiable. Missing phase and multi-fan Expected Results, support limits and safety envelope prevent execution now but are ordinary Project readiness inputs, not a permanent review blocker.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains the operator-plus-telemetry concept but expands beyond its one-fan command to the actual BIOS and multi-fan scope and rejects exposed credentials.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation and adds explicit criteria-coverage accounting, Disabled-phase independent protection and final BIOS readback.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic PARTIAL handling with per-state/per-combination evidence and recovery.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Keeps the conditional class while distinguishing incomplete Criteria from source contradiction and protecting simultaneous removal under disabled shutdown.

review_improvement: Makes the dangerous BIOS-disabled multi-fan sequence auditable without inventing PASS criteria, and prevents a single-fan readout from masking unsupported combination or restoration gaps.
independent_technical_reasoning: Thermal Shutdown state changes the consequence of the same cooling loss, while fan1 and fan2+fan3 affect different redundancy margins. Because the operation and explicit fan1 direction are understandable, engineers can supply the missing matrix and limits. Physical actions remain manual, telemetry is automatable, and readiness—not permanent blocking—is the correct V3.1 treatment.
